Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.question: 1) The germ cell from which the ovum is ultimately derived is:
Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.exp: Oogonia proliferate during fetal life and give rise to primary oocytes.

Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.question: 2) The mature Graafian follicle ruptures under the influence of:
Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.exp: The mid-cycle LH surge triggers ovulation.

Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.question: 3) Ovulation usually occurs approximately:
Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.option1: 14 days before the next menstrual period
Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.option2: On the first day of menstruation
Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.exp: Ovulation occurs about 14 days before the onset of the next menstrual cycle.

Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.question: 4) The principal hormone secreted by the corpus luteum is:
Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.exp: Progesterone maintains the secretory endometrium after ovulation.

Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.question: 5) The normal site of fertilization is the:
Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.exp: Most fertilizations occur in the ampullary portion of the fallopian tube.

Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.question: 6) Implantation normally occurs:
Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.exp: The blastocyst implants about one week after fertilization.

Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.question: 7) The hormone detected by pregnancy tests is:
Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.exp: Pregnancy tests detect β-hCG produced by trophoblastic tissue.

Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.question: 8) The primary source of progesterone during the first trimester is the:
Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.exp: The corpus luteum maintains early pregnancy until placental hormone production is established.

Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.question: 9) The uterine artery is a branch of the:
Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.exp: The uterine artery arises from the anterior division of the internal iliac artery.

Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.question: 10) The broad ligament is formed by:
Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.exp: It is a double fold of peritoneum extending from the uterus to the pelvic wall.

Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.question: 11) The ovarian ligament connects the ovary to the:
Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.exp: The ovarian ligament attaches the ovary to the uterine cornu.

Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.question: 12) The main function of the fallopian tube is:
Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.option1: Fertilization and transport of the ovum
Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.exp: Fertilization occurs in the tube, which also transports the embryo to the uterus.

Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.question: 13) The endometrium reaches its maximum thickness during the:
Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.exp: Progesterone causes maximal endometrial development after ovulation.

Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.question: 14) The dominant estrogen produced during the reproductive years is:
Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.exp: Estradiol (E2) is the principal estrogen in reproductive-age women.

Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.question: 15) The normal menstrual cycle length is approximately:
Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.exp: Although normal cycles vary, 28 days is the classic average.

Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.question: 16) A 26-year-old woman has a regular 28-day menstrual cycle. Ovulation is most likely to occur on:
Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.exp: In a 28-day cycle, ovulation usually occurs around day 14.

Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.question: 17) A woman undergoes laparoscopic sterilization. Which structure is occluded?
Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.exp: Female sterilization is achieved by occluding the fallopian tubes.

Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.question: 18) A woman has an ectopic pregnancy located at the commonest site. Which part of the tube is involved?
Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.exp: Approximately 70% of tubal ectopic pregnancies occur in the ampulla.

Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.question: 19) A patient has failure of ovulation because there is no mid-cycle LH surge. Which event will not occur?
Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.exp: Without an LH surge, ovulation and corpus luteum formation do not occur, preventing the secretory phase.

Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.question: 20) A woman becomes pregnant after successful fertilization. Which structure first secretes hCG?
Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.exp: Syncytiotrophoblast cells begin secreting hCG soon after implantation.

Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.question: 21) The ovarian cycle is primarily regulated by:
Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.exp: GnRH, FSH, and LH regulate follicular development and ovulation.

Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.question: 22) Which hormone is primarily responsible for proliferation of the endometrium?
Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.exp: Estrogen stimulates endometrial proliferation during the follicular phase.

Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.question: 23) A woman presents with primary ovarian failure. Which hormone level is expected to be elevated?
Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.exp: Loss of ovarian negative feedback leads to elevated FSH levels.

Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.question: 24) Which structure prevents reflux of menstrual blood from the vagina into the uterine cavity?
Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.exp: Menstrual blood normally flows outward through the cervical canal; there is no specific anatomical reflux-prevention structure.

Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.question: 25) A woman with regular menstrual cycles undergoes endometrial biopsy on day 22. Which histological feature is expected?
Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.option3: Secretory glands with subnuclear vacuoles and tortuosity
Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.exp: The luteal phase produces a secretory endometrium under the influence of progesterone.

Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.question: 26) The hormone responsible for development of the dominant follicle is:
Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.exp: FSH stimulates growth and maturation of ovarian follicles during the follicular phase.

Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.question: 27) The normal pH of the vagina in reproductive-age women is approximately:
Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.exp: Lactobacilli produce lactic acid, maintaining an acidic vaginal environment.

Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.question: 28) The most important organism responsible for maintaining normal vaginal acidity is:
Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.exp: Lactobacilli convert glycogen into lactic acid, maintaining vaginal pH.

Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.question: 29) The outer epithelial covering of the ectocervix is:
Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.exp: The ectocervix is lined by stratified squamous non-keratinized epithelium.

Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.question: 30) The endocervical canal is lined by:
Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.exp: The endocervix contains mucus-secreting columnar epithelium.

Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.question: 31) The squamocolumnar junction is clinically important because it is the common site for:
Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.exp: Most cervical intraepithelial neoplasia and cervical cancers arise in the transformation zone.

Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.question: 32) The functional layer of the endometrium is supplied mainly by:
Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.exp: Spiral arteries undergo cyclic changes and are shed during menstruation.

Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.question: 33) The basal layer of the endometrium is retained during menstruation because it is supplied by:
Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.exp: Straight arteries supply the basal layer, allowing regeneration after menstruation.

Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.question: 34) The average volume of menstrual blood loss is:
Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.exp: Normal menstrual blood loss ranges from 20 to 80 mL.

Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.question: 35) The dominant ovarian follicle usually measures approximately _ just before ovulation.
Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.exp: A mature Graafian follicle is typically 18–24 mm in diameter before ovulation.

Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.question: 36) A 24-year-old woman has regular menstrual cycles. Ultrasound on day 13 shows a 21-mm follicle. What is the most likely event within the next 24–48 hours?
Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.exp: A follicle measuring about 18–24 mm is usually ready to ovulate.

Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.question: 37) A cervical biopsy shows transformation zone epithelium. This zone represents the junction between:
Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.exp: The transformation zone is where columnar epithelium is replaced by squamous epithelium.

Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.question: 38) A woman presents with infertility due to bilateral tubal blockage. Fertilization normally occurs in which structure?
Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.exp: The ampulla is the usual site of fertilization.

Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.question: 39) Following ovulation, the ruptured follicle transforms into the corpus luteum under the influence of:
Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.exp: LH induces luteinization of granulosa and theca cells.

Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.question: 40) A woman with pituitary failure has low LH and FSH levels. Which ovarian function is most directly impaired?
Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.exp: Gonadotropins are essential for follicular growth and ovulation.

Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.question: 41) The ovarian cortex primarily contains:
Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.exp: Ovarian follicles are located within the cortex.

Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.question: 42) The ovarian medulla mainly contains:
Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.exp: The medulla provides vascular and neural support to the ovary.

Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.question: 43) Which hormone causes thinning of cervical mucus around ovulation?
Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.exp: Estrogen produces thin, watery cervical mucus favorable for sperm penetration.

Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.question: 44) The fern pattern seen in cervical mucus is due to high levels of:
Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.exp: Estrogen increases sodium chloride content, producing the characteristic ferning.

Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.question: 45) Basal body temperature rises after ovulation because of the thermogenic effect of:
Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.exp: Progesterone increases basal body temperature by approximately 0.3–0.5°C.

Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.question: 46) A woman tracking fertility notices a sustained rise in basal body temperature. This indicates:
Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.exp: Basal body temperature rises after ovulation due to progesterone.

Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.question: 47) A woman has abundant, clear, stretchy cervical mucus. She is most likely in the:
Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.exp: Estrogen peaks around ovulation, producing copious, elastic cervical mucus.

Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.question: 48) The uterine muscle layer responsible for contractions during labor is the:
Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.exp: The myometrium consists of smooth muscle responsible for uterine contractions.

Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.question: 49) The peritoneal covering of the uterus is known as the:
Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.exp: The perimetrium is the outer serosal layer of the uterus.

Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.question: 50) A woman with regular cycles experiences ovulation but no implantation. The corpus luteum will typically regress after approximately:
Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.exp: In the absence of pregnancy, the corpus luteum regresses about 14 days after ovulation.

Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.question: 51) The hormone responsible for maintenance of pregnancy during the first trimester is:
Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.exp: Progesterone produced by the corpus luteum maintains the endometrium until placental takeover.

Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.question: 52) Placental progesterone production becomes sufficient to maintain pregnancy by approximately:
Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.exp: The luteo-placental shift occurs around 8–10 weeks of gestation.

Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.question: 53) The principal estrogen produced by the placenta during pregnancy is:
Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.exp: Estriol is the major estrogen synthesized by the fetoplacental unit.

Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.question: 54) Human placental lactogen (hPL) is mainly responsible for:
Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.exp: hPL promotes insulin resistance, ensuring glucose availability for the fetus.

Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.question: 55) The main source of oxytocin is the:
Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.exp: Oxytocin is synthesized in the hypothalamus and released from the posterior pituitary.

Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.question: 56) Which hormone is primarily responsible for milk synthesis?
Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.exp: Prolactin stimulates milk production in the mammary glands.

Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.question: 57) The milk ejection reflex is mediated by:
Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.exp: Oxytocin contracts myoepithelial cells, causing milk let-down.

Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.question: 58) The ovarian hormone that exerts negative feedback on FSH secretion is:
Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.exp: Inhibin produced by granulosa cells selectively suppresses FSH secretion.

Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.question: 59) The endometrium is shed because of withdrawal of:
Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.exp: Regression of the corpus luteum causes withdrawal of ovarian steroids, leading to menstruation.

Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.question: 60) The menstrual phase usually lasts:
Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.exp: Normal menstrual bleeding usually lasts 3–5 days.

Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.question: 61) A woman with hyperprolactinemia presents with amenorrhea. The elevated prolactin suppresses secretion of:
Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.exp: Hyperprolactinemia inhibits hypothalamic GnRH, reducing FSH and LH secretion.

Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.question: 62) A postpartum woman is unable to breastfeed despite normal nipple anatomy. Which hormone deficiency is most likely?
Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.exp: Prolactin deficiency results in failure of milk production.

Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.question: 63) A breastfeeding mother has normal milk production but poor milk ejection. Deficiency of which hormone is most likely?
Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.exp: Oxytocin is essential for milk ejection but not milk synthesis.

Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.question: 64) A woman has a pituitary adenoma causing excessive prolactin secretion. Which menstrual abnormality is most likely?
Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.exp: Hyperprolactinemia suppresses ovulation, leading to amenorrhea.

Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.question: 65) A woman has absent menstruation despite normal estrogen levels because the endometrium fails to respond to progesterone. Which phase of the menstrual cycle will be absent?
Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.exp: Progesterone converts the proliferative endometrium into the secretory endometrium.

Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.question: 66) A patient undergoes hysterectomy. Which ligament contains the uterine artery and is clamped during surgery?
Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.exp: The uterine artery runs within the base of the broad ligament near the cardinal ligament.

Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.question: 67) During hysterectomy, the ureter is at greatest risk of injury where it passes:
Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.exp: Water under the bridge—the ureter passes beneath the uterine artery.

Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.question: 68) A surgeon accidentally ligates the uterine artery without injuring the ureter. The uterine artery normally crosses:
Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.exp: The uterine artery crosses superior to the ureter near the cervix.

Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.question: 69) A woman with cervical carcinoma requires radical hysterectomy. Knowledge of which anatomical relationship is most important to avoid ureteric injury?
Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.option4: Ureter lateral to external iliac artery
Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.exp: To avoid Fistula formation

Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.question: 70) A woman has bilateral ovarian artery ligation during pelvic surgery. The ovarian arteries arise directly from the:
Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.exp: The ovarian arteries originate directly from the abdominal aorta below the renal arteries.

Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.question: 71) The lymphatic drainage of the ovary primarily follows the ovarian vessels to the:
Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.exp: Ovarian lymphatics drain to the para-aortic nodes because of their embryological origin.

Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.question: 72) The primary lymphatic drainage of the cervix is to the:
Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.option4: Pelvic (internal/external iliac and obturator) lymph nodes
Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.exp: The cervix primarily drains to pelvic lymph nodes.

Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.question: 73) The normal adult uterus is usually:
Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.exp: The uterus normally lies anteverted over the bladder and anteflexed on the cervix.

Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.question: 74) The strongest support preventing uterine prolapse is provided by the:
Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.exp: The cardinal ligament is the principal support of the cervix and upper vagina.

Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.question: 75) The pelvic floor muscle that provides the major dynamic support to the pelvic organs is:
Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.exp: The levator ani forms the principal muscular support of the pelvic viscera.

Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.question: 76) A multiparous woman develops uterine prolapse due to weakness of the pelvic floor. Which muscle is primarily affected?
Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.exp: Damage to the levator ani is a major cause of pelvic organ prolapse.

Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.question: 77) A woman undergoes surgery for ovarian cancer. The first regional lymph nodes assessed for metastasis are the:
Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.exp: Ovarian lymphatic drainage is primarily to the para-aortic nodes.

Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.question: 78) A hysterosalpingogram demonstrates free spill of contrast into the peritoneal cavity. This indicates:
Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.exp: Free peritoneal spill confirms tubal patency.

Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.question: 79) A woman with infertility undergoes hysterosalpingography showing bilateral cornual obstruction. Which part of the tube is affected?
Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.exp: Cornual obstruction refers to blockage of the intramural (interstitial) segment.

Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.question: 80) A surgeon performing abdominal hysterectomy identifies the ureter crossing beneath the uterine artery before ligation. This relationship is classically remembered as:
Anatomy & Physiology of Reproduction.exp: The ureter (water) passes beneath the uterine artery (bridge)—
